- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.4) or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 2–3 days ahead.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high forecast vs low true, adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → less correction, lower → more.
